_note: RETROSPECTIVE historical cases for PRISM risk validation (V2.1 Phase 3). These are NOT predictions made at the time: initial-evidence inputs are reconstructed approximations from public historical records, clearly labeled retrospective. Outcomes are documented history. Sample is far too small for statistical calibration claims.

cases.what_happened: Container ship Ever Given grounded in the Suez Canal, blocking the corridor for six days (March 2021).
cases.initial_evidence_reconstructed: Multiple independent reports confirmed an active full corridor blockage; salvage underway with uncertain timeline; ~12% of global trade transits the canal.

ai_likelihood.outcome: continued corridor closure with global shipping delays

cases.subsequent_outcome: Canal reopened after 6 days; hundreds of ships delayed; measurable global trade and freight-cost impact; no long-term structural change.

cases.what_happened: Houthi attacks on Red Sea shipping from late 2023 forced major carriers to reroute around the Cape of Good Hope.
cases.initial_evidence_reconstructed: Confirmed attacks on multiple vessels; several major carriers announced rerouting; insurance costs rising; sustained campaign indicated.

ai_likelihood.outcome: sustained rerouting with higher freight costs and delays

cases.subsequent_outcome: Rerouting persisted for months; transit times +10-14 days; freight rates spiked; disruption materialized as anticipated.

cases.what_happened: Russia-Ukraine war disrupted Black Sea grain exports from February 2022; later partially mitigated by the Black Sea Grain Initiative.
cases.initial_evidence_reconstructed: Confirmed port closures and naval activity; Ukraine and Russia are major wheat exporters; conflicting reports on export continuity.

ai_likelihood.outcome: grain export shortfall with global price pressure

cases.subsequent_outcome: Wheat prices spiked to record levels; exports fell sharply until the July 2022 corridor deal; impact materialized.

cases.what_happened: Francis Scott Key Bridge collapsed after a container ship strike (March 2024), closing the Port of Baltimore for weeks.
cases.initial_evidence_reconstructed: Single confirmed catastrophic incident; port closure announced; vehicle and coal shipments affected; national impact limited.

ai_likelihood.outcome: weeks-long port closure with regional logistics disruption

cases.subsequent_outcome: Port reopened ~11 weeks later; regional disruption real but national impact contained; materialized at anticipated scale.

cases.what_happened: Drought lowered Gatun Lake levels; Panama Canal Authority cut daily transits through 2023-2024.
cases.initial_evidence_reconstructed: Official transit restrictions announced; drought conditions verified; gradual rather than sudden disruption; some conflicting forecasts on duration.

ai_likelihood.outcome: reduced canal capacity with rerouting and delays

cases.subsequent_outcome: Transits cut by ~a third; queues and auction fees soared; rains restored capacity in 2024; disruption materialized.

cases.what_happened: Announced review of possible new tariffs on a major trading partner (2023); measures were largely not implemented within the horizon.
cases.initial_evidence_reconstructed: Single-source announcement of a review; no enacted measures; officials signaled negotiation; thin detail on scope.

ai_likelihood.outcome: possible new tariffs affecting import costs

cases.subsequent_outcome: No broad tariffs enacted within 90 days; talks continued; anticipated disruption did NOT materialize.
